svg.title: CausalLab: same observations do not fix an intervention
svg.desc: Supplied finite structural models, exhaustive enumeration. Association is positive .26 while the interventional difference is negative .10. Two observationally identical models give intervention probabilities 1 and .5; shared-noise counterfactual probabilities 1 and 0 given factual X0,Y0. These are synthetic mechanism assumptions, not learned real-world causes.

svg.text: Exhaustive finite worlds under supplied mechanisms. Probability scale 0..1 in every panel.
Synthetic model counterexamples, not effects learned from observational data or policy advice.
P(Y under X=1 is 1 | factual X=0,Y=0)
Factual evidence fixes U=0 in both.
Reusing U is not drawing fresh noise.
One observational distribution does not identify the causal mechanism. The equations are assumptions.
Observation selects worlds; action replaces an equation; counterfactual prediction reuses factual noise.
Full models, probability values, factual/action traces and fixed domains are embedded in metadata.
